newsitem.title: GERMANY: German think-tank predicts natural gas boom.
newsitem.headline: German think-tank predicts natural gas boom.

text.p: Natural gas use is booming in Germany and has excellent long-term prospects, especially in the developing eastern states, the Bavarian think-tank Ifo said on Sunday.
Natural gas use rose 10 percent in 1995, partly due to a particularly cold winter, and should show even stronger growth by the end of 1996, the institute said in its latest report.
The glowing long-term sales outlook justified German natural gas providers' spending of 6.6 billion marks ($4.33 billion) in 1995 and an estimated 6.2 billion marks in 1996, Ifo said.

Spending by providers was likely to decline, however, with major networks now in place in western Germany and the build-up of systems in the eastern states largely complete. Average annual investment from 1997 through 1999 would be around 5.6 billion marks.
Ifo noted that the opening of the eastern states had created a larger market for German natural gas sales and that use in the region had climbed by a third from January to September this year.
By 2020, natural gas use in Germany as a whole would be more than 40 percent higher than the level in 1992. ($1=1.5250 Mark)
